text:
viv: quick flag from the weekend int4 deployment - we're seeing recall drop on the deid-longtail-recall holdout for chunked docs. Not a huge latency win, but measurable quality loss (~2.7% recall). Need a targeted microgolden + kernel fingerprinting.

Tomas: can you paste the eval and the slices showing the worst drop?

viv: pasted: 
```
$ rbin eval --model q4b-2.1-int4 --dataset deid-longtail-recall --slices chunked_docs,multi-table
Recall@k: 74.3% (-2.7% vs fp16)
Precision@k: 81.2% (-1.1%)
Hallucination-rate: 6.0% (+1.2%)
Latency p50: 220ms
```

nora: interesting. any obvious config delta on kv-cache or batching?

viv: default serving config. quick ablate toggling kv-cache -> tiny +0.2% recall, so not the main driver. We saw some correlation with a specific attention kernel permutation in the stress runs but not 100% repro.

ash: we should treat as a quality regression. Proposal: focused microgolden of 300 examples: 180 long chunked docs (>=900 tokens), 80 multi-table documents, 40 synthetic paraphrase edgecases. 3 labelers per item. Also capture fingerprints and dedupe against existing gold.

Tomas: agree. also run a kernel-variant fingerprint sweep so we can tie which kernel/permute combo correlates with recall drop. Example command: 
```
rbin quant-sweep --model q4b-2.1 --bits 4 --kernels aten,flash,fast_attn --permute none,block,row --kv-cache on,off --eval deid-longtail-recall --save logs/q4b-2.1-kernelfingerprint
```

labeler-bot: New ticket ML-4600 created: "q4b-2.1-int4: recall drop on deid-longtail-recall". Labeling plan attached.

nora: I'll kick off the sweep and attach per-run kernel fingerprints (kernel_name+permute+shard_checksum) to ML-4600. If a single kernel variant consistently recovers recall we can pin it for Dedicated routes.

viv: dataset assembly plan: sample 1.2k recent RAG sessions -> run 5-gram shingle fuzzy dedupe -> fingerprint -> surface 500 candidates -> labeler queue -> finalize 300. Provenance fields: source_ts, session_id, md5_text, shingle_hash, route.

ash: labeler checklist (ops copy):
1) confirm required source segments are present
2) check retrieval recall: are the expected evidence passages returned in any order?
3) mark missing passages as 'recall-miss' and provide evidence ids
4) mark hallucinated passages as 'hallucination' with smallest evidence span
5) severity 0-3

ops-bot: Labeling batch LB-8202 created for ML-4600. Estimated ETA for first pass: 60 hrs.

Tomas: for the console, let's add a short-lived dashboard card "deid-longtail recall (int4-regressions)" tracking Recall@k on golden + prod, with a 24-hr rolling regression alarm. Also export the microgolden fingerprints for quick regression detection.

nora: sweep started. I'll attach kernel trace logs and the kernel fingerprint CSV to ML-4600/logs when done.

viv: ash, can you own dedupe + candidate export? please push artifacts to ML-4600/artifacts and create LB-8202 payload.

ash: on it. plan: fuzzy dedupe threshold 0.82, shingle size 5, then filter out any sample in the existing golden index by md5_text. Will add an automated provenance manifest.

labeler-bot: LB-8202 populated with 500 candidates staged -> awaiting labeling assignment.

viv: recap/action items: (1) nora run kernel sweep + upload fingerprints/logs to ML-4600, (2) ash assemble/dedupe/export candidates + populate LB-8202, (3) labelers run LB-8202 and finalize 300 microgolden, (4) tomas/console add dashboard card and alert. Ping here for blockers. :white_check_mark:
